THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for the respondent-State.

2. The factual matrix of the case of the prosecution before the Trial Court is that accused was working as Second Division Clerk in Mujarayi Section of Tarikere Tahsildar office from 12.01.1995 to 02.06.1998.
On 03.10.1996, he has withdrawn Rs.8,032/- as payment to Archaka of Ranganathaswamy Temple for the period from July 1970 to October, 1996.
Again on 03.01.1997, he has withdrawn Rs.10,029/- as payment to Archaka Basappa from July 1970 to January, 1997.
Thereby, he has withdrawn double the amount for the same period.

Similarly, he has withdrawn Rs.10,048/- towards payment to Archaka of Hanumantha Temple of Duglapura relating attached to Mujarayi Department on 01.10.1996 for the period from July 1970 to January, 1990.
Again on 06.12.1996, he has withdrawn Rs.18,000/- as payment to Archaka by name of Govindappa for the period from July 1970 to December 1996.
On verification, it is found NC: 2024:KHC:10756 that accused has not paid the amount either to Basappa or Govindappa.

The accused has created documents with an intention to cheat the Government and gain wrongfully without making payment to the Archaka of Ranganathaswamy Temple of Chakonahalli and Hanumantha Temple of Duglapura.
3. The police have investigated the matter and filed the chare-sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 468, 471, 409 and 420 of IPC and the accused was secured and he has not pleaded guilty.
Hence, the prosecution examined the witnesses as P.Ws.1 to 16 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P33.
The revision petitioner has not adduced any evidence before the Trial Court.

4. The Trial Court having considered both oral and documentary evidence available on record,
convicted the accused for the offence punishable under Section 468 and imposed sentence of 3 months and fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for two months.

The accused was sentenced to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- for the offence under Section 471 of IPC, in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for two NC:
2024:KHC:10756 months.

Further, he was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.1,200/- for the offence punishable under Section 409 of IPC, in default Shekarappa R vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120650195/
2 of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for three months.

sentences.text: The accused was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for three months and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- for the offence under Section 420 of IPC, in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for three months.

Being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and sentence, an appeal is filed in Crl.A.No.152/2014.
5.

The First Appellate Court, on reassessing the evidence available on record, particularly the evidence of P.W.4 with regard to the handwriting of the accused and also evidence P.W.5, who is the panchanama witness and the document at Ex.P24, observed that accused has admitted the fact that he was working as Second Division Clerk and he has withdrawn the amount to pay Thastik amount to Archakas and he has agreed to re-deposit the same and he has paid the excess amount.
That document was not disputed during the cross-examination of P.W.1.
The Trial Court also taken note of the evidence of P.Ws.7, 15 and 13.

The First Appellate Court NC: 2024:KHC:10756 also, having considered the grounds urged in the appeal memo, considering the evidence of P.Ws.1 to 4 and 5 and so also the evidence of P.Ws.7 and 15, who is the Handwriting Expert, who has compared the disputed handwriting and admitted handwriting, confirmed the judgment of the Trial Court.
Being aggrieved by the concurrent finding, the present revision petition is filed.

6. The main contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that both the Courts committed an error and in the absence of any FSL report that the documents which have been created are not in the handwriting of the appellant, ought not to have convicted the accused, which leads to miscarriage of justice.

Learned counsel also would contend that the complainant has conducted its own enquiry, on verification, it is found that he had prepared a false case against the accused and this petitioner is made as scapegoat.

In the absence of any documentary evidence and also the handwriting in the documents which have been seized at the instance of the petitioner prove that he only prepared the document and misappropriated the amount, the Trial Court would have taken into consideration the aspect of failure on the part of the NC: 2024:KHC:10756 prosecution in getting the report from the Handwriting Expert and committed an error in not considering the same and committed grave error in accepting the case of the prosecution.

It is contended that the First Appellate Court also committed an error in appreciating both oral and documentary evidence placed on record and both the Courts proceeded in an assumption that accused pleaded guilty and the evidence of each of the prosecution witnesses is inconsistent, artificial and exaggerated and when there were number of unexplained facts did not explain the prosecution theory, both the Courts committed an error in convicting the accused.

7. Per contra, learned HCGP would submit that the witnesses P.Ws.5, 6, 7 and 9 have categorically deposed with regard to the drawing up of mahazar and seizure of documents and also collection of specimen signature.

It is contended that P.Ws.1 and 2 are also the mahazar witnesses and witnesses,
particularly P.Ws.5, 6, 7 and 9 have supported the case of the prosecution.

It is also contended that P.W.13 has also supported the case of the prosecution, who is an Handwriting Expert and both the Courts have not committed any error in convicting and sentencing the petitioner.

Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for the respondent-State,
this Court has to analyze the evidence of the prosecution witnesses available on record.

P.W.1 is only a mahazar witness in respect of Ex.P1- mahazar under which the documents are seized in the presence of P.W.1 and he supported the case having seized the document and obtained the signature in the mahazar.
It is also his evidence that Tahsildar has sent the document to the Police Department from his office.
P.W.1 is the Shirastedhar of Taluka Kacheri and though he turned hostile partially, no cross- examination with regard to the seizure of documents in terms of Ex.P1 from the office of the Tahsildar.
The defence did not dispute the said fact.
9. The prosecution also examined P.W.2, who is also a signatory to mahazar, Ex.P1 and he identifies his signature as Ex.P1(b).
He also categorically says that police have seized the documents and taken his signature.

This witness was also partially treated hostile by the prosecution and accused persons have not disputed the document of Ex.P1.
NC: 2024:KHC:10756 10.
The other witness is P.W.3, who is a panch witness in respect of Ex.P2-mahazar.
He identifies his signature as Ex.P2(a) and also admits and identifies his signature in Ex.P3 as Ex.P3(a).
He also categorically says that Ex.P4 is the handwriting of the accused and he identifies his signature as Ex.P4(a) and so also signature Ex.P5(a) and Ex.P6(a).
This witness was also treated hostile and cross-examined by the learned Public Prosecutor and defence have not cross-examined this witness.

11. P.W.4 is a panch witness and he identifies his signature as Ex.P2(b), Ex.P3(b), Ex.P4(b),
Ex.P5(b) and Ex.P6(b).
This witness is treated hostile by the prosecution and accused persons have not disputed the signature.

12. P.W.5 is the retired Tahsildar and the prosecution mainly relied upon the evidence of retired Tahsildar and in his evidence, he categorically says that an amount of Rs.8,092/- was paid to Sri Ranganathaswamy Archaka Basappa for the period from July 1970 to October, 1996 and an amount of Rs.10,079/- was paid for the period from July 1970 to January 1997 which was found in the audit report and notice was given NC: 2024:KHC:10756 to Archaks Basappa and came to know that no such Basappa was working.
Then came to know about misappropriation of the amount.

In respect of proceeding of Sri Hanumantha Devara Temple for the period from July 1970 to January 1996, an amount of Rs.10,048/- was paid and also for the period from July 1970 to January 1996, an amount of Rs.18,000/- was paid and when notice was given to Govindappa, he denied that he has not received the amount and also notice was given to the petitioner, but he did not repay the amount which he has misappropriated.
Hence, complaint was given on 03.11.2003 along with audit report.

He also produced service records of the petitioner and also the receipts for having paid Thastik amount to the Temple which are marked as Exs.P8 and P9 and so also letter given by the Convener to his office as Ex.P10 and Archaka of Chakonalli also gave the letter in terms of Ex.P11 and so also letter dated 22.12.1996 given by Basappa is marked as Ex.P12.
For having made the payment in favour of Archaka Basappa to the tune of Rs.10.079/- on 03.01.1997, receipt is produced as Ex.P13.

The Office Tippani is marked as Ex.P14 and the receipt for having paid the amount of Rs.8,032/- to the Archaka Basappa is marked as Ex.P15 and Shekarappa R vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120650195/
4 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:10756 also Office Tippani dated 01.10.1996 to release the amount is marked as Ex.P16.

sentences.text: The Archaka Govindappa gave the letter on 22.09.1996 and the same is marked as Ex.P17 and also the letter for payment towards Archaka Govindappa is marked as Ex.P18.
The Office Tippani is marked as Ex.P19 and so also Office Tippani dated 06.10.1996 is marked as Ex.P20.

The Convener Virupaksha letter is marked as Ex.P21 and on 22.10.1996, the said Archaka Govindappa has given the letter in terms of Ex.P22 and Ex.P23 and the statement of Govindappa is marked as Ex.P24.
The notice issued to the petitioner is marked as Ex.P25 and final notice as Ex.P26.
Ex . P27
is the reply to letter dated 18.12.2000 and passbook are marked as Exs.P28 and P29.

The receipt allegedly given by Govindappa for having received the amount of Rs.10,048/- on 01.10.1996 is marked as Ex.P30, the receipt dated 06.12.1996 allegedly issued by Govindappa is marked as Ex.P31 to the tune of Rs.18,000/-.
In the cross-examination of P.W.5, he admits that the said Govindappa has not given any complaint and he cannot tell on what date the said Govindappa has given the requisition for the first time.
However, he says that in - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:10756 terms of the audit report, he asked the accused to repay the amount.

13. The other witness is P.W.6, who is the Second Division Assistant, who took the charge from the accused- Shekarappa and he also speaks with regard to the misappropriation of amount of Rs.10,098/- and Rs.8,032/- and also misappropriation of the amount in respect of other temple to the tune of Rs.10,098/- and Rs.8,032/-.
It is also the evidence that they have given notice to the Archaka and Archaka Govindappa comes and says that he has not received any amount.
In the cross-examination of this witness also, nothing is elicited, except making the suggestion that said Govindappa did not give any complaint.
He admits that, during audit time, passbooks were given.
14. The other witness is P.W.7, who is the State Accounts, F.D.A.

In his evidence, he categorically says that when audit was done, he noticed the payment made in 1996- 97 and 1997-98 and in all,
Rs.80,000/- was misappropriated in terms of six Cheques and there was entry for having made payment to Ranganatha Temple and details of Archaka and - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:10756 drawing of amount and encashment of the said amount is mentioned.
In respect of other temple i.e., Guddapura Temple also, there was misappropriation.
This witness was subjected to cross-examination.

He says that during the audit for the said period of two years, this petitioner was working and suggestion that he was not working was denied.
15.
The other witness is P.W.8, who is also First Division Assistant of Zilla Panchayath for having done the audit work from 1996-1998.

sentences.text: The other witness is P.W.9, who is the retired Government employee.

He speaks with regard to the payment made in favour of some of the temple and states that he used to take the bills for treasury for the period from 1970 to 1996 and also other periods and by that time, this petitioner was working.
He came to know about taking of money when the audit work was done.

In the cross-examination of this witness also, a suggestion was made that amount was taken by the Archaka of Ranganatha Temple and Hanumantha Temple and the said Archakas have not given any complaint.
The other witness is P.W.10.
He is not the material witness and he is a retired Village Accountant.

18. The other witness is P.W.11, who is a Second Division Assistant of Taluka Office, who continued the work of the accused and he speaks with regard to the misappropriation and registering of criminal case.
19. The other witness is P.W.12-ASI, who received the complaint and registered the case.
20. The other witness is P.W.13-CPI, who collected the specimen signature and also details of service records of the petitioner.
21. The other witness is P.W.14, who is the ASI, who took the seized documents and gave the same to the FSL.

22. The other witness is P.W.15, who is the Assistant Director of FSL and he says with regard to the receipt dated 01.10.1996 for amount of Rs.10,048/- and the said receipt was given by said Govindappa and his opinion is that the same is not signed by Govindappa and he cannot tell, who signed the - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:10756 said document.

The receipt is marked as Ex.P30 and the other receipt is marked as Ex.P31.
23.
The other witness is P.W.16, who is the CPI, who investigated the matter and filed the charge-sheet.

24. Having perused both oral and documentary evidence placed on record, it is not in dispute that the documents are seized at the office of the Tahsildar, mahazar was drawn in terms of Ex.P1 and the same is not denied by the petitioner when the signatures of particular witnesses are also marked and have been reported and the signature is marked as Ex.P1(b) and the witnesses of P.Ws.2, 3 and Shekarappa R vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120650195/
6 4 are the mahazar witness in respect of Exs.P3 to P5.

sentences.text: The material witness is the P.W.5 i.e., the retired Tahsildar, who gave the report for having made the payment for the period from 1970 to 1996 in respect of both the temples.
He categorically says that documents are marked at his instance when the same were seized.
In the cross-examination of this witness, except eliciting the answer that on what date Archaka Govindappa gave the complaint, he did not say anything with regard to the passbook.
He also admits that Exs.P7 to P31 are not prepared in his presence.

The other witness is P.W.6, who is the official witness of the Tahsildar office and P.W.7 though he supported the case of the prosecution that there was a misappropriation of amount and bills are raised in 1996-1997, it is not in dispute that during the said period, this petitioner was working.
P.W.7 is also part of the audit and P.W.9 is also a retired official, who speaks with regard to the payment of amount for the period from 1970- 1996,
that too during the period when the petitioner was working in the same department.

25. It is important to note that though there is a seizure of documents and the Handwriting Expert gives opinion i.e., P.W.15 that the receipts which have been seized i.e., Ex.P30 and Ex.P31 not contains the signature of said Govindappa and specimen signature are taken from the petitioner, it is the opinion of the Expert that he cannot vary such opinion whether the receipts are signed by the petitioner or not.

Apart from that, the case of the prosecution is that amount was paid to Archakas Govindappa and Basappa and those two persons have not been examined before the Trial Court and the allegation of the prosecution is also that amounts are paid in favour of Govindappa and Basappa,
they have only examined the - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:10756 persons, who conducted the audit and persons, who have worked during that period.

No doubt, there is a misappropriation of amount for the period from 1970 to 1996 and in order to come to a specific conclusion that the same is done by the petitioner himself, no material is placed on record.

Merely because, the petitioner was working in the same department in the same section, unless the material is produced before the Court with regard to his act of misappropriation is concerned, the petitioner cannot be convicted.

Further the Handwriting expert opinion is also not specific with regard to this petitioner is concerned and while convicting an accused for the serious offence under Section 409 IPC and other offences in criminal prosecution, there must be cogent evidence.

26. Though prosecution made efforts to prove the same, but the very persons i.e., Govindappa and Basappa are not examined before the Trial Court and they are the crucial witnesses and the prosecution only relied upon the statements.

It is also important to note that the Trial Court while passing the order in Para No.21 of the judgment made an observation that accused-Shekarappa has given statement before the - 17 - Shekarappa R vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120650195/
7 NC: 2024:KHC:10756 Assistant Commissioner and he has admitted misappropriation of amount of Rs.80,000/- and undertakes to redeposit the amount and also agreed to deduct Rs.1,000/- every month from his salary month for misappropriating the amount and the said statement is not forthcoming in the records, though the same is marked and the Trial Court only made an observation, but no such statement before the Court.
The prosecution relies upon the document of Ex.P27 stating that the petitioner has given reply.
But, on perusal of reply also, he has not admitted with regard to the misappropriation of the amount, but only he has said some mistake has crept in.
27. While convicting the accused, there must be cogent evidence before the Trial Court.
The Trial Court in Para No.21 committed an error in relying upon the alleged statement made before the Assistant Commissioner and no such document is available before the Court.

The First Appellate Court also not analyzed the material on record, though discussed in Para Nos.11 to 15 with regard to the material collected by the prosecution and in Para No.15, comes to the conclusion that P.W.15 is the Expert, who has compared the disputed handwriting with admitted handwriting and observed that from - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:10756 the evidence of P.W.15, the prosecution is able to prove Exs.P30 and P31 are not the receipts given by Govindappa, who is the Archaka of the Temple.

Even if the Court comes to the conclusion that those receipts are not in the handwriting of Govindappa, at the same time, the same are not in the handwriting of the petitioner and no specific and cogent evidence that those receipts are created by the petitioner herein.

28. When such being the case, the same has not been analyzed by the First Appellate Court and the Court comes to the conclusion that accused has given no explanation and unless the material discloses that the same is in the handwriting of the accused, the question of giving any explanation does not arise and erroneously, the First Appellate Court comes to the conclusion that evidence of P.Ws.16 and 5- complainant and opinion of the Expert are sufficient to prove the case of the prosecution and the said approach of the First Appellate Court is erroneous and the evidence of the Handwriting Expert is not clear, except stating that Exs.P30 and P31 are not in the handwriting of said Basappa and nothing is pointed out towards the petitioner herein.

Hence, the First - 19 - NC: 2024:KHC:10756 Appellate Court also committed an error in appreciating both oral and documentary evidence placed on record and comes to the conclusion that the petitioner himself misappropriated the amount and the evidence based on record is not sufficient to convict the accused for the offence punishable under Sections 468, 471, 409 and 420 of IPC and unless the fact that the documents are in the handwriting of the accused and made use by the petitioner for misappropriation is proved, the petitioner cannot be convicted and both the judgments passed by the Trial Court and the First Appellate Court suffers from its legality and correctness and it requires interference by exercising the revisional powers.
Hence, the order impugned passed by the Trial Court and the First Appellate Court requires to be set aside.

When such being the case, the same has not been analyzed by the First Appellate Court and the Court comes to the conclusion that accused has given no explanation and unless the material discloses that the same is in the handwriting of the accused, the question of giving any explanation does not arise and erroneously, the First Appellate Court comes to the conclusion that evidence of P.Ws.16 and 5- complainant and opinion of the Expert are sufficient to prove the case of the prosecution and the said approach of the First Appellate Court is erroneous and the evidence of the Handwriting Expert is not clear, except stating that Exs.P30 and P31 are not in the handwriting of said Basappa and nothing is pointed out towards the petitioner herein.
Hence, the First - 19 - NC: 2024:KHC:10756 Appellate Court also committed an error in appreciating both oral and documentary evidence placed on record and comes to the conclusion that the petitioner himself misappropriated the amount and the evidence based on record is not sufficient to convict the accused for the offence punishable under Sections 468, 471, 409 and 420 of IPC and unless the fact that the documents are in the handwriting of the accused and made use by the petitioner for misappropriation is proved, the petitioner cannot be convicted and both the judgments passed by the Trial Court and the First Appellate Court suffers from its legality and correctness and it requires interference by exercising the revisional powers.
